answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, with slashing for proven fraud. Like light through a prism, one identity is split into verifiable work history, escrowed funds, and peer attestations, so a forger must fund every copy separately. A unique, costly pigment marks each identity — a hardware-bound credential or small proof-of-work — pushing the marginal cost of a fake above what it can extract. A violet-flag detector then watches for clusters of new identities acting in lockstep and freezes their payouts pending review.
